project.name: ExplainableAI-MicrocyticAnemia-CDS
project.title: Explainable AI for Microcytic Anemia Classification — Rich Terminal App

what_runs_locally: All ML model training (scikit-learn, XGBoost, LightGBM, Optuna tuning)
what_uses_llm_backend: CBC value extraction from PDF text
CBC value extraction from images (vision model)
architecture_clarification.why_local_training_is_fine: 16GB RAM + decent CPU can train XGBoost + Optuna (50 trials, 5-fold CV) on 1500 rows in under 5 minutes. No GPU needed for tabular CBC data.
architecture_clarification.llm_backend_is_swappable: All LLM calls go through a single LLMClient class in modules/llm_client.py. Switch between Groq and Ollama by changing one setting in config.py or from the Settings menu at runtime.

files.main.py: Rich terminal app — main menu loop

modules/.llm_client.py: SINGLE unified LLM interface — Groq or Ollama, swappable at runtime
modules/.data_generator.py: Synthetic CBC dataset generation via LLM backend
modules/.data_loader.py: Load and validate real CSV datasets
modules/.ui_components.py: All Rich panels, tables, banners, menus
modules/.settings_manager.py: Runtime settings: switch LLM backend, model name, temperature

models/.model_metadata.json: Model name, F1, training date, dataset info

llm_client.description: The most important module. ALL LLM calls in the entire project go through this one class. Never call Groq or Ollama directly anywhere else.

usage_in_other_modules.pattern:
from modules.llm_client import LLMClient
client = LLMClient(backend=config.LLM_BACKEND)
response = client.chat(prompt)
data = client.chat_json(prompt)
result = client.vision(image_path, prompt)
usage_in_other_modules.rule: Never import groq or call requests to Ollama directly. Always use LLMClient.

content.LLM_BACKEND: 'groq'  # Change to 'ollama' to switch. Also changeable from Settings menu at runtime.

settings_menu.description: Runtime settings panel accessible from main menu. No restart needed when switching backends.

If model not installed: show command 'ollama pull llama3.2' and wait
on_switch_to_groq: Show which Groq models will be used

ollama_setup_guide.description: Embedded in the app — shown when user selects Ollama for first time

steps.note: Run this in a separate terminal. Keep it running while using HematoAI.
llama3.2 is 2GB. llava vision model is 4.7GB. Both run fine on 16GB RAM.

steps.how: Main Menu → Settings → LLM Backend → ollama

model_size_guide.note: With 16GB RAM you can run llama3.1:8b + llava simultaneously comfortably.

training_strategy.clarification: ML training (XGBoost, Random Forest, Optuna) runs entirely locally on your machine. 16GB RAM is more than sufficient. Groq/Ollama is NOT used for training — only for LLM text tasks.

expected_training_time.note: XGBoost on tabular data is CPU-efficient. No GPU needed.

models_trained_locally: XGBoost (primary — best for tabular medical data)

data_generation.prompt: Generate a realistic synthetic CSV of 1500 microcytic anemia patients. Columns: patient_id,age,gender,Hb,MCV,MCH,MCHC,RBC,RDW,Hematocrit,label. Classes: IDA 60% (RDW high >15, RBC low-normal, MCV 60-79), Thalassemia_Trait 30% (RDW normal <15, RBC high >5.0, MCV very low 60-75), Anemia_of_Chronic_Disease 10% (MCV 72-85, RBC low). Add Gaussian noise. Include 15% borderline overlap. Output ONLY raw CSV starting with header row. No markdown, no explanation.

pdf_cbc_extraction.prompt: Extract CBC values from this lab report text. Return ONLY a JSON object with exactly these keys: Hb, MCV, MCH, MCHC, RBC, RDW, Hematocrit. Use null for missing values. Ignore units. Text: {text}

image_cbc_extraction.step_1: Preprocess with OpenCV: grayscale + threshold + denoise
image_cbc_extraction.step_3: If OCR output < 80 chars or contains no numbers: use vision model
image_cbc_extraction.vision_prompt: This is a medical CBC lab report. Extract these values and return ONLY JSON: {Hb, MCV, MCH, MCHC, RBC, RDW, Hematocrit}. Use null for missing. Numbers only, no units.

eda_narrative.prompt: Given per-class CBC statistics: {stats_json}. As a hematologist, give 4 bullet points: (1) top discriminating parameters between IDA and Thalassemia Trait, (2) what RDW pattern reveals, (3) what RBC count pattern reveals, (4) dataset quality assessment. Plain language for a GP.

clinical_explanation.prompt: Patient CBC: {cbc_values}. ML prediction: {predicted_class} ({confidence:.1f}% confidence). Derived indices: Mentzer={mentzer:.2f} ({'IDA pattern' if mentzer>13 else 'Thalassemia pattern'}), Shine-Lal={shine_lal:.1f}, England-Fraser={ef:.2f}. Top 5 SHAP features: {shap_features}. As a clinical hematologist, in exactly 3 sentences: (1) why this CBC pattern fits this diagnosis, (2) which single parameter is most diagnostic and why, (3) the most critical next step for a rural GP with limited resources. Be direct. No jargon.

how_to_use_this_prompt.message_to_paste: You are an expert Python ML engineer. Build this entire project from the JSON spec below. Create every file in the project_structure exactly as described. The most important module is modules/llm_client.py — implement it exactly as specified in the llm_client section including the full Python code. All other modules must use LLMClient for every LLM call. ML training runs locally using scikit-learn/XGBoost/Optuna. The Rich terminal UI in main.py is the only interface. Start by creating config.py, then llm_client.py, then main.py, then all other modules.
how_to_use_this_prompt.step_5: Install Tesseract OCR separately: sudo apt install tesseract-ocr (Linux) or download from GitHub for Windows
how_to_use_this_prompt.step_6: Add GROQ_API_KEY to .env (get free at console.groq.com)
how_to_use_this_prompt.step_8: Select 6 to generate synthetic data and train
how_to_use_this_prompt.step_10: Later: go to Settings (S) to switch to Ollama when ready

meta.key_design_principle: One LLMClient class controls everything. Swapping Groq for Ollama (or back) is a single runtime toggle — no code changes, no restart required.
meta.training_runs: locally on your 16GB machine — fast, offline, no API cost
meta.llm_runs: on Groq cloud now, Ollama later — both through identical LLMClient interface
meta.internet_required: Only when using Groq backend. Ollama mode is fully offline.
